headline: Across two multi-note clinical tasks, a TF-IDF baseline is never worse than a 110M domain-pretrained transformer, and MLM pretraining of a from-scratch encoder contributes nothing measurable downstream.
matched_protocol: identical chars/note for every system; verified 372.8 vs 374.5 tokens and 6.16 vs 6.14 notes consumed; best-epoch-on-val; LR grid; paired DeLong + bootstrap on identical val rows

pretraining_effect.note: both under the correct recorded input convention and a decontaminated corpus; both inside the +/-0.008 seed noise

mlm_vs_downstream: a 1.32 +/- 0.015 nat MLM gap produces a downstream AUROC difference of ~0.002
provenance_verdict: falsified three ways: role is 98.9% recoverable from text at the model window (<=0.098 bits); the bias is exactly inert on single-provenance input; an arbitrary segment ordinal outperforms true role labels
retractions: 0.22 AUROC gap between TF-IDF and PubMedBERT was a harness bug (neural arms read 1.39 of 6.78 notes); true matched gap is 0.050
ours_pretrained < ours_random was an input-convention mismatch, not a pretraining effect
open: locked test set never touched (6,776 mortality / 6,155 readmission examples)
token and label ladders built but not run
4 of 7 pretraining arms not carried downstream
single seed reported per selected LR
RETRACTED: See results/RETRACTION_floor_unmatched.json -- the floor in this file was unmatched (full text vs a 63-token/note neural cap). Corrected gaps: mortality +0.002, readmission -0.018 (PubMedBERT wins).
